War Rules

A card game of pure luck for two: the higher card wins, and a tie means war.

The rules

The cards
32 cards: 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King and Ace in four suits. The Ace is highest; the suit does not matter. Each player gets 16 cards as a face-down pile.
A round
Both players turn up the top card of their pile. The higher card wins both cards, and they go under the winner's pile.
War
If both cards are equal, it's war: each player puts one card face down and one face up. The higher face-up card takes all the cards on the table. If they are equal again, the war goes on.
Running out
A player with only one card left in a war turns it up without a face-down card. A player with no card left to turn up loses the game.
Short or to the end
Short (the default): after 30 rounds the player with more cards wins; with the same number it's a draw. To the end: play until one player has all 32 cards. So that a long game cannot go round in circles, won cards go under the pile in random order, and after 2000 rounds the game ends in a draw.
Playing here
You play against the computer. There are no decisions: tap your pile, and both cards are turned up. The table shows the round, with face-down war cards as striped backs, and both piles show how many cards they have.

A war

The picture shows a war: both players turned up a 9; after one face-down card each, the King beats the 8.
